notes: Only the three included documents (CITL, Grainger guidance, Grainger Using AI) were coded; course documents were deferred. Main disagreement kinds: (1) unit_stance on permitted-use statements (permit vs encourage) and on rationale or consequence sentences (restrict vs neutral); resolved by whether the sentence sets a limit or only explains. (2) phase and actor where the passage's context decided (for example the course-materials paragraph is addressed to instructors; sanction sentences are when-misuse). (3) modality for explanatory sentences (informs vs should or must), settled by the wording. (4) policy_type: UNCOVERED vs a nearby type (citation examples to P24 with a fit_note; applications-style warning to P94 with a fit_note), P36 over P19 for the 'considered plagiarism' sentence, P01 over P05 for a named-assignment ban, P32 over P41 for CITL's aim. Coder A found 16 units B did not and B found 4 A did not; 18 of 20 were kept as real policy statements, two (a Fluency Certificate link, a pointer to the College of Law samples) were dropped as navigation. One A unit B folded into a neighbour (debugging limit) was kept separately. Pairing was by position in the source; a few automatic pairings were corrected by hand. agree_unit_stance is also reported.
